final_assessment: R-crc-11 amended by Sal with (h) effort is RECORDED never TARGETED and (i) the user frames and guardrails, the AI solves — correcting a call I had got wrong, since I was about to drop the pass and finding counts entirely rather than keep them as evidence. Testing the amendment instead of asserting it produced two findings. First, effort is ALREADY recorded and merely unread: a full profile for every archived change (passes by class, walks, findings per pass, elapsed span) was derived from existing .orbit-runs/ trails with zero instrumentation, so the deliverable is a reading surface rather than a recording obligation — cheaper, retroactive, and with no new field anyone can forget to write. Second, the first reading immediately yielded a diagnostic nobody had stated: findings-per-pass going back UP is the signature of a walk having invented mechanism, with converged changes monotonic (c1: 5,0,0,0) and ground ones oscillating (rc07: 12,8,5,10,5, the jump at pass four being an external reviewer finding defects in code the previous walk had just written). The cost shape was then ratified — {tokens, tool_uses, source} per PASS and per WALK, with provenance inside the unit because a fresh subagent yields a harness number, an external pass yields a human transcription, and anything in-context yields nothing honest. The asymmetry is written down rather than left to be discovered: walks run in-context by design, so the most expensive activity is the least measurable, and an all-unavailable walk column must never be read as walks being cheap. Tokens are named explicitly as the field this ruling will be tested on, being the most targetable number a development process can hold. Q-crc-18 is resolved. One observation recorded short of a ruling: this is the third write-only record found in two days — gate_overridden, the residual in a warnings string, and the effort profile — so orbit is better at writing records than at reading them; a fourth instance would earn a ruling.
